name: Coming of Age Day
venue: Citywide · photo crowds at Meiji Jingu
desc: National holiday. New adults in furisode and formal wear; ceremonies and photo crowds across Tokyo, especially at Meiji Jingu.

name: Dezome-shiki firefighters
desc: New Year firefighters’ parade: trucks, ladder acrobatics, band, water displays. Outdoor seats are reserved; indoor exhibits are easier to drop into.

name: Daikon Radish Festival
desc: Temple offers cooked furofuki daikon and sake after a memorial service. Free, short, good add-on to Asakusa.

name: Grand Sumo Hatsu Basho
desc: January tournament runs 10–24 Jan. Days in this window: Sun 10 and Mon 11. Tickets sell out. Top-division bouts late afternoon.

name: Tondoyaki bonfire
desc: Ceremonial burning of New Year decorations. Drums, “Tondo!” chants, roast mochi. Smoke is said to mean good health. Free. Weather can cancel.

name: Hashigo-nori ladders
desc: Traditional firefighter ladder stunts during temple ceremonies. A smaller local version of the Big Sight Dezome-shiki.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Yanaka)
desc: Walk seven shrines or temples and collect goshuin stamps (~¥300 each). Yanaka is the quieter old-town route.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Nihonbashi)
desc: One of the shortest lucky-gods circuits, in the old merchant district. Free entry; stamps extra.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Asakusa)
desc: Compact pilgrimage around Senso-ji. Easy with kids who like a stamp scavenger hunt.

name: Seven Lucky Gods (Kameido)
desc: Eastern Tokyo circuit starting at Kameido Tenjin. Plum trees may be budding later in January.

name: Ueno antique market
desc: Aozora Kotto-ichi: antiques, ceramics, kimono, old books, vintage clothes. Free to browse. Pair with Ueno Zoo.

name: GUNDAM-Con 2027
desc: Gundam 50th-anniversary convention: exhibits, stages, Gunpla and game championships. Paid lottery tickets. Official cosplay rules apply.

name: Cinnamoroll Park
desc: Sanrio indoor park with a ~12 m Cinnamoroll slide, photo spots, and games. Timed tickets. Strong pick for a 10-year-old.

name: Tokyo Mega Illumination
desc: Large winter light show plus miniature horses and ponies (photos ~17:30–19:00). Cold outdoor evening — wear layers.

name: Tokyo Disney Resort
desc: Disneyland and DisneySea. Book tickets ahead and check parade hours. Full-day outing next to Tokyo.

name: Ghibli Museum
desc: Cat Bus (small kids only), short film, rooftop robot. No indoor photos. Lawson tickets from 10 Dec 2026. Often closed Tuesdays — 5 Jan is a Tuesday.

name: Midtown Ice Rink
desc: Largest outdoor real-ice rink in central Tokyo. Gloves required; rental extra. Penguin sleds for small kids. Weekday evenings are quieter.

name: Meiji Jingu Gaien rink
desc: Full-size indoor rink. Weather-proof. Ticket plus rental about ¥2,200 on weekdays.

name: Tatsumi Ice Arena
desc: Tokyo’s largest indoor arena, two rinks. Closed 1 Jan and usually the third Monday. 10 min from Tatsumi Station.

name: Winter Wonder Park
desc: Harbor-side rink (resin last season). Ages 3+. Last season about ¥1,200 including rental. Pair with Chinatown.

name: Shin-Yokohama Skate Center
desc: International-size indoor rink and cheap public sessions. Easy if you are already on that side of Yokohama.

name: Yoyogi Forest of Lights
desc: Walk through trees with light and sound. Calmer than Mega Illumination. Good after Harajuku or Meiji Jingu.

name: Marunouchi Illumination
desc: Champagne-gold trees from Tokyo Station toward the palace. Free evening street walk.

name: Hibiya Magic Time
desc: Entertainment-district winter lights. Pair with a nearby concert or an Imperial Palace walk.

name: Ebisu Garden Place lights
desc: Covered courtyard lights. Indoor-adjacent if the weather is rough.

name: Relaxing Aquarium Dream Day
desc: Special daytime program (moved from 2026). Regular highlights: tuna tank, penguins, sea birds. Details usually posted in December.

name: Ueno Zoo
desc: Children’s zoo, elephants, polar bears, shoebill. No giant pandas. Cheap metropolitan tickets. Pair with the antique market.

name: Tama Zoological Park
desc: Larger, more spacious African and Asian gardens. Better if you want a quieter full-day zoo.

name: Inokashira Park Zoo
desc: Birds, small mammals, guinea pigs. Combine with Inokashira Park or the Ghibli Museum.

name: Sumida Aquarium
desc: Penguins and jellyfish. Compact, about 1.5–2 hours. Easy with Skytree.

name: Sunshine Aquarium
desc: Shorter visit with rooftop penguin tanks. Handy if you are already in Ikebukuro.
